newsitem.title: FRANCE: In reversal, Paris to let people walk on grass.
newsitem.headline: In reversal, Paris to let people walk on grass.

text.p: In a policy reversal, Paris plans to let people walk on the grass.
City hall said on Wednesday it would take down signs saying "Keep off the grass" in the capital's 413 public gardens to give Parisians an unprecedented chance to walk, play or loll on the lawns.
"The capital is not a museum and we want to give the public back the lawns in Paris," a city hall official said.
Under the scheme, Parisians would be allowed access to part of the grass in each park, while another section is roped off to let the grass recover.
The municipality also planned to set up chairs and benches in the capital's parks, which cover 3,000 hectares (7,400 acres), and make special provisions for the handicapped.
Paris has some of the best manicured lawns of any major city, but under current by-laws anyone venturing onto the grass gets ordered off. The most awkward offenders can be fined.
